assertions.name: C1_positive_root_COUNTS_match_the_known_values
assertions.source: A1..A5, D4, D5, E6, E7, E8 all reproduce (10 checked); the generator is not inventing its own root systems

assertions.name: C2_every_generated_union_has_the_RANK_it_was_asked_for
assertions.source: so 'edges = rank - components' is applicable; ADE diagrams are trees, which is what makes the arrow count a function of the type alone

assertions.name: C3_the_enumeration_is_EXHAUSTIVE_at_each_rank
assertions.source: rank->#types {2: 2, 3: 3, 4: 6, 5: 9}: rank 2 gives A1+A1, A2; rank 3 gives A1^3, A1+A2, A3; rank 4 adds A2+A2, A1+A3, A4, D4. A target is therefore hit by exactly one type or by none — there is nothing to choose

assertions.name: every_reading_gives_a_UNIQUE_Dynkin_type
assertions.source: all four (rank, spectrum) pairs are hit by exactly one ADE type. The arrow count is not chosen — it is read off

assertions.name: the_TWO_KNOT_reading_is_unique_but_answers_the_WRONG_QUESTION
assertions.source: abelian-is-a-node -> {'4_1': 0, '5_2': 0}, abelian-is-not -> {'4_1': 1, '5_2': 1}: both unique. Kept because the calculation is correct, LABELLED because the corpus's target is not two knots' totals

assertions.name: CORRECTED_the_arrow_count_is_NOT_FORCED
assertions.source: with total = 7 the arrow count is [0, 1, 2] across ranks 4-7: rank 4 = A1+A3 (2 arrows); rank 5 = A1+A2+A2 (2 arrows); rank 6 = A1+A1+A1+A1+A2 (1 arrows); rank 7 = A1+A1+A1+A1+A1+A1+A1 (0 arrows). V must be pinned first, and nothing in the corpus pins it

assertions.name: and_the_MERGED_node_result_does_NOT_pin_V
assertions.source: C_irr = [trace field : Q] is a PER-KNOT count; the target is ONE quiver spanning the bar-conjugate ray pair, so its V is a different quantity. The chain 'rank = node count' was broken from the start under the corpus's reading — that is the substantive half of the error, not the arithmetic

assertions.name: HOW_THE_ERROR_HAPPENED_and_it_was_flagged_by_its_own_author
assertions.source: the first version listed (A5) 'the recorded DT count is the indecomposable count' as an assumption AND named it the first thing to check before building on the result. It was wrong, and checking it took one grep of the bean. Flagging a weak assumption is not the same as testing it

description: qou-q9ih D1-b, the arrow question -- and this probe CORRECTS ITS OWN FIRST VERSION, which concluded 'the arrow count is FORCED to 0 or 1'. That answered the wrong question. The Gabriel lever is sound and is kept: for an acyclic quiver with W=0, finite type <=> simply-laced Dynkin, #indecomposables = #positive roots, and every ADE diagram is a TREE so a rank-V union with k components has V-k edges. What was wrong is which (rank, spectrum) pairs it was fed. The first version read the target (4,3) as TWO KNOTS' total spectra with rank = the per-knot C_irr. The bean says otherwise in as many words: 'Target object: (Q, W, ray+, ray-) -- quiver with potential plus TWO stability rays, ray-wise DT counts (4,3)'. So (4,3) are ray-wise counts of ONE quiver, and the coincidence C(4_1)=3, C(5_2)=4 is what made the misreading available. Two things break: stable objects have a definite slope so the ray sets are DISJOINT and the total is >= 7; and rank is no longer the per-knot node count at all, so the merged C_irr result does not pin V. Corrected result: V >= 4 and total >= 7, and if the spectrum is exactly the two rays then arrows = 2 at ranks 4-5, 1 at rank 6, 0 at rank 7. THE ARROW COUNT IS NOT FORCED -- V must be pinned first and nothing in the corpus pins it. A constraint table, not a resolution. The two-knot reading is still computed and still unique, labelled as the answer to a question the corpus did not ask. Exact integers; no floats. Scope-(a); nothing wired; no fit.

assumption_chain.A1_W_zero: the corpus's M2 finding (AomegaM2BPSCohomology, lean-direct exit 0)
assumption_chain.A3_finite_spectrum: LOAD-BEARING; an infinite spectrum means non-Dynkin and nothing is forced
assumption_chain.A4_simply_laced: Gabriel covers quivers; B/C/F/G need valued quivers and are excluded, not overlooked
assumption_chain.A5_DT_count_is_indecomposable_count: if the corpus's (4,3) are per-ray counts of one quiver instead, the total is >=7 and A1+A3 becomes the candidate

scope.tier: scope-(a), conditional on the assumption chain
scope.method: exhaustive ADE enumeration + exact positive-root counts; no search against the target, no fit
